name: Dehydrated Skin
description: Dehydrated skin lacks sufficient moisture, leading to a dull appearance and other issues such as fine lines and sensitivity. It is different from oily or dry skin types and requires specific care to manage effectively.
causes: Dehydration from internal sources (not drinking enough water)
symptoms: Dryness and flakiness of the skin
Loss of elasticity and appearance of fine lines
Tight feeling, especially after washing or applying products
risk_factors: Frequent exposure to wind or cold weather
Use of air conditioning and central heating
recommended_product_categories: Sunscreen with high SPF to protect from environmental damage

daily_routine.purpose: Gentle removal of impurities without stripping the skin's natural oils
Balances the skin’s pH and prepares it for better absorption of serums and moisturizers
Provides concentrated hydration and anti-aging benefits
Locks in moisture to keep the skin hydrated throughout the day
Prevents further dehydration from UV rays

professional_treatments: Intense hydration facials with hydrating masks and serums
Laser therapy to improve skin texture and reduce the appearance of fine lines
Microdermabrasion or chemical peels to exfoliate and refresh the skin
natural_remedies: Using a humidifier in dry environments
Eating foods rich in omega-3 fatty acids (e.g., fish, flaxseeds)
lifestyle_tips: Limiting exposure to harsh environmental conditions
common_myths: Dehydrated skin is the same as dry skin. (In fact, they are different and require different treatments.)
Applying heavy creams will block pores and make the skin feel worse. (Lightweight hydrating products can be effective without clogging pores.)
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite home care or if there is an increase in irritation, redness, or pain.

severity_levels.mild: Visible dry patches and tightness but no significant irritation or discomfort.
severity_levels.moderate: Dryness, flakiness, and some redness with occasional itching.
severity_levels.severe: Severe dryness leading to cracking, bleeding, and intense sensitivity.

expert_tips: Regularly assess your skin type and adapt your skincare routine accordingly.
Consult a dermatologist for personalized advice on addressing specific concerns.
